title.narrative: 16th replenishment of the African Development Fund

description.narrative:
In 2024 the total resource envelope for the 2023–2025 period of the 16th replenishment of the ADF (ADF-16) amounted to UA 6,230 million. This included donor contributions of UA 3,785 million,7 concessional donor loans of UA 427 million, and an advanced commitment capacity of UA 2,018 million. Total subscriptions received by December 2024 amounted to UA 3,838.54 million. By 31 December 2024, the Fund had received UA 76.91 million9 as payment to the UA 313 million Climate Action Window, which was part of ADF-16.
Read more in the 2024 Annual Report (Released 27 may 2025): https://www.afdb.org/en/documents/annual-report-2024
Based on the AfDB’s Annual Development Effectiveness Review, the following results can be reported in relation to select Danish priorities as set out in the Organisation Strategy – for all African countries and for ADF countries, respectively.
Climate change and green growth: Improved ‘installed renewable capacity’, ‘new renewable power capacity installed’, ‘emission reductions in energy’, ‘people with new or improved access to water and sanitation’ as well as ‘new operations with climate informed design’. Deteriorated ‘people with new electricity connections’ whereas ‘access to electricity’ and ‘access to at least basic drinking water services’ remains the same, while the latter is still below the 2015 baseline.
Level 1: ‘Access to electricity’: all African Countries: remained at 56 %. ADF: up from 41 to 44 %.
‘Installed renewable capacity’: all African countries: up from 54 to 56 GW. ADF: up from 26 to 27 GW.
‘Access to at least basic drinking water services’: all African countries: remained at 69 %. ADF: remained at 59 %.
Level 2: ‘New renewable power capacity installed’: all African countries: up from 72 to 113 MW. ADF: up from 56 to 78 MW.

The 16th replenishment of the African Development Fund (ADF-16) operational 2023-2025 will strengthen the Fund as a strategic partner for low-income African countries. Its guiding vision is of a climate-smart, resilient, inclusive, and integrated Africa. It is built on two pillars: Sustainable, climate-resilient and quality infrastructure; and Governance, capacity building and sustainable debt management. Gender equality and private sector development remain essential cross-cutting issues. ADF-16 is backed by a pipeline of more than 300 operations and additional climate actions.
